entry.title: Ravda Beach, Nessebar
entry.summary: Ravda is a quieter resort village south of Nessebar with a long sandy beach and shallow water. It is more relaxed than Sunny Beach, with a mix of hotels, restaurants and local life.

entry.title: Velvet Strand, Portmarnock
entry.summary: The Velvet Strand is a long beach of firm, smooth sand north of Dublin, with views to Ireland's Eye and Lambay Island. In 1930 Charles Kingsford Smith took off from here on a transatlantic flight.

entry.title: Curracloe Beach
entry.summary: Curracloe is a long sandy beach on the Wexford coast, backed by dunes and Raven Wood. Its opening scenes stood in for Omaha Beach in the film Saving Private Ryan. The south-east is one of the sunniest corners of Ireland.

entry.title: Rossnowlagh Beach
entry.summary: Rossnowlagh is a long, wide beach of firm sand on Donegal Bay, popular with surfers and families. Gentle, consistent waves make it one of the best places in Ireland to learn to surf.

entry.title: Lahinch Beach
entry.summary: Lahinch is a lively surf town with a long sandy beach on Liscannor Bay, and the Cliffs of Moher are a short drive away. Several surf schools work from the promenade, and the waves suit both beginners and experienced surfers.

entry.title: Barleycove Beach
entry.summary: Barleycove is a wide sandy bay backed by high dunes near Mizen Head, the most south-westerly point of Ireland. A river estuary crosses the beach, and the dunes are a protected habitat.

entry.title: Derrynane Beach
entry.summary: Derrynane has white sand and clear water in a sheltered bay on the Ring of Kerry, next to Derrynane House, the home of Daniel O'Connell, now a national historic park. At low tide you can walk to Abbey Island and its ruined abbey.

entry.title: Coumeenoole Beach, Slea Head
entry.summary: Coumeenoole is a small sandy cove at the western tip of the Dingle Peninsula, reached by a steep path from the Slea Head Drive, with views to the Blasket Islands. The setting is spectacular, but the currents here are strong.

entry.title: Inch Beach
entry.summary: Inch Beach is a sand spit about 5 km long reaching across Dingle Bay, with dunes behind and mountains on every side. Gentle surf makes it a good place to learn, and it featured in films such as Ryan's Daughter.

entry.title: Dog's Bay, Roundstone
entry.summary: Dog's Bay is a crescent of brilliant white sand made largely of tiny shells, on one side of a narrow sandy neck. Gurteen Bay lies on the other side, so you can choose the more sheltered beach on a windy day.

entry.title: Keem Bay, Achill Island
entry.summary: Keem Bay is a horseshoe of pale sand and clear blue-green water at the western end of Achill Island, enclosed by steep green hills. The road down is narrow and winding, with sweeping views over the Atlantic.

entry.title: Swinoujscie Beach
entry.summary: Swinoujscie has a very wide beach of fine white sand on the Polish side of Usedom, with a long promenade that continues into Germany towards Ahlbeck. The town sits on several islands, linked by ferries and a road tunnel.

entry.title: Miedzyzdroje Beach
entry.summary: Miedzyzdroje is a popular resort on the island of Wolin, with a wide sandy beach, a pier and a seafront promenade. To the east, tall cliffs and beech forest belong to Wolin National Park, home to a small bison reserve.

entry.title: Kolobrzeg Beach
entry.summary: Kolobrzeg is one of the largest spa towns on the Polish coast, with a long sandy beach, a pier and a red-brick lighthouse at the harbour mouth. Spa hotels and parks line the seafront.

entry.title: Ustka Beach
entry.summary: Ustka is an old fishing port with sandy beaches on both sides of the harbour, a lighthouse and a long promenade. The eastern beach is the main resort area, and the western beach is quieter.

entry.title: Leba Beach
entry.summary: Leba is a busy resort town with a broad beach of very fine white sand. Just west of town is the Slowinski National Park, a UNESCO biosphere reserve famous for moving sand dunes, the highest about 40 m.

entry.title: Debki Beach
entry.summary: Debki is a small village with a wide, natural beach of fine sand and dunes, where the Piasnica river flows into the Baltic. It is popular with young people and families who want a simpler holiday than in the big resorts.

entry.title: Jurata Beach
entry.summary: Jurata is the smartest village on the Hel Peninsula. You can choose between the open-sea beach with waves on the north side and the calm, shallow Bay of Puck on the south side, where a pier runs out into the water.

entry.title: Hel Beach
entry.summary: The Hel Peninsula is a narrow 35 km spit of sand between the open Baltic and the Bay of Puck. On the sea side, the beach near the town of Hel is wide and backed by pine forest, and the town has a seal centre run by the University of Gdansk.

entry.title: Orlowo Beach and Cliff
entry.summary: Orlowo is a quieter beach in Gdynia, below the Orlowo Cliff, a wooded clifftop nature reserve with views across the Bay of Gdansk. A small pier and fishing huts sit at the southern end.

entry.title: Sopot Beach
entry.summary: Sopot has a wide sandy beach between Gdansk and Gdynia, with the 511 m wooden pier, the longest in Europe, and the grand 1920s Grand Hotel right on the sand. The resort is lively in summer, with bars and clubs along the seafront.

entry.title: Travemunde Beach
entry.summary: Travemunde is the seaside quarter of Lubeck, with a sandy beach and promenade at the mouth of the Trave. Large ferries to Scandinavia pass the beach, and the four-masted barque Passat is moored as a museum ship across the river.

entry.title: Timmendorfer Strand
entry.summary: Timmendorfer Strand is one of the best-known resorts on the Bay of Lubeck, with a long beach of fine sand, a promenade and smart hotels. The water is calm and shallow, which suits families.

entry.title: Prerow Beach
entry.summary: Prerow has a long, wide beach of fine sand backed by dunes and woods, on the edge of the Western Pomerania Lagoon Area National Park. The village is a quiet holiday spot of thatched houses, and a new pier with a ferry stop opened in 2024.

entry.title: Weststrand, Darss
entry.summary: The Weststrand is a long natural beach inside the Western Pomerania Lagoon Area National Park, backed by forest where storms have bent the trees into strange shapes. There are no buildings, no bars and usually very few people.

entry.title: Ahlbeck Beach
entry.summary: Ahlbeck has a broad beach of fine white sand in front of its famous pier, described as the oldest in Germany, with a pavilion with green turrets. The Polish border and Swinoujscie are a short walk along the sand.

entry.title: Heringsdorf Beach
entry.summary: Heringsdorf is one of the three Imperial Spas (Kaiserbader) on Usedom, with fine white sand, grand villas and a 508 m pier opened in 1995, the longest in Germany. A promenade runs along the coast to Ahlbeck and Bansin.

entry.title: Kuhlungsborn Beach
entry.summary: Kuhlungsborn is a classic Baltic resort with a long sandy beach backed by a seafront promenade, villas and a pier. Groynes break up the shore into sections, and the water is shallow near the beach.

entry.title: Warnemunde Beach
entry.summary: Warnemunde has a very wide beach of fine sand next to the old lighthouse and the Teepott building, at the mouth of the river Warnow. Cruise ships and ferries pass close by on their way to Rostock, which makes it a lively place to watch the sea.

entry.title: Prora Beach
entry.summary: Prora beach runs for kilometres along the Bay of Prorer Wiek, with fine white sand and pine woods behind it. Behind the trees stands the huge unfinished Nazi-era holiday complex, now partly turned into flats, hotels and a youth hostel, with a documentation centre on its history.
